title: t6: fixed symbol lookup on the second-to-last token (head 0.1 -> mlp0)
label: verified
behavior: BOS + 5 tokens from {ge, pe, ro, sa, zu}; the model outputs one symbol at the last position.
summary: The model outputs M[x4], where x4 is the fourth input symbol (token position 4, the one just before the last) and M is the fixed table ge->pe, pe->zu, ro->ge, sa->sa, zu->ro. All other inputs, including the last token itself, are ignored. Head 0.1 is a pure previous-token head that copies the position-4 token to the last position; mlp0 then applies the lookup and writes the answer. Heads 0.0 and 0.2 play no part. All numbers are from the local-full backend (full precision). Held-out verification: 300/300 agreement, circuit ablated -> metric -0.002 (accuracy 20%, chance), everything else ablated -> metric 1.0 (accuracy 100%).
pseudocode:
def predict(tokens, prompt):
    # tokens = [BOS, x1, x2, x3, x4, x5]
    moved = tokens[4]                      # head 0.1: last position attends to position 4 (E0012, E0010)
    M = {2: 3, 3: 6, 4: 2, 5: 5, 6: 4}     # mlp0 lookup (E0006): ge->pe, pe->zu, ro->ge, sa->sa, zu->ro
    return M[moved]

claims.text: The model reproduces the dataset answers on 100% of prompts (the behaviour is deterministic and clean).

The output is a fixed lookup of the token at position 4: ge->pe, pe->zu, ro->ge, sa->sa, zu->ro. The rule agrees with the model on 300/300 held-out inputs (null agreement with shuffled labels: mean 0.20, max 0.25).
Before layer 0 only position 4 matters: patching the clean residual at position 4 into a corrupt run recovers 100% of the metric gap, every other position 0%.
After layer 0 the answer is entirely at the last position (resid_post at position 5 recovers 100%, position 4 recovers 0%).
Head 0.1 is necessary and is a previous-token head: mean-ablating it leaves 0.3% of the metric, and its attention from position 5 to position 4 is 1.0.
mlp0 is necessary: mean-ablating it leaves 0.8% of the metric; patching clean mlp_out (all positions) into a corrupt run recovers 100%.
Heads 0.0 and 0.2 play no part: ablating both together leaves 100% of the metric, and with everything except {0.1, mlp0} ablated the model keeps 100% accuracy.

The circuit {0.1, mlp0} is necessary and sufficient on held-out data: ablated -> fraction of clean -0.002 and accuracy 0.203; alone -> fraction 1.0 and accuracy 1.0; all effects beat their null distributions.

nodes.label: mlp0: lookup table M at position 5

limitations: Two pre-registered predictions were scored inconclusive because the metric path I registered does not exist in the result (E0004, E0013). The observed values (0.0075 and 1.0) match the hypothesis; E0004 was re-tested on a new sample as E0009 with the same threshold.
The lookup table was read from the model's input/output pairs, not decoded from mlp0's weights or neurons; how the 15 MLP neurons implement the table was not studied.
mlp_out patching covers all positions at once, so 'mlp0 acts at position 5' is inferred from E0011 (only position 5 matters after the layer), not measured per position.
No path patching was run to show directly that 0.1's output is what mlp0 reads; this follows from both being individually necessary and jointly sufficient in a one-layer model.
open_questions: What do the distractor heads 0.0 and 0.2 write, and into which subspace, given that it never reaches the output?
How is the table distributed over mlp0's neurons?
